Out-of-sample validation of mixed-model RESI: Tennessee STAR

mlmRev::star hybrid plasmode: point-estimate calibration and CI coverage

2026-11-16

1 Purpose

The mixed-model RESI point estimator, its Lyu–Welsh targets and the confidence intervals of notes/resi_mixed_ci.qmd were developed and checked on mlmRev::egsingle. This report repeats the same hybrid plasmode on a dataset they were not developed on, to check that nothing in the methods or the simulation framework is tuned to egsingle. The code is shared: hybridPlasmodeSim(), lyuLimitResi(), expectedDesignResi(), designAveragedSe() and resi() in the package, and tests/mixed_ci_coverage_lib.R for the coverage summaries. Only the data preparation (tests/star_data.R) and the driver (tests/run_star_validation.R) are new.

2 Dataset and model

mlmRev::star is the Tennessee STAR class-size experiment: yearly mathematics scores (kindergarten to grade 3) for students nested in schools, the same occasion < student < school nesting as egsingle but with far fewer occasions per student and different kinds of covariates.

Complete cases on the model variables
Quantity Value
schools 80
students 11009
measurements 23982
students per school (min / median / max) 54 / 126 / 362
measurements per student (mean) 2.18

Model (fitted by ML to the full data; the fit is the data-generating truth):

math ~ yrs + sx + black + ses + cltype + schtype3 + fl_10 + (1 | sch/sid)

  • yrs: years in the study (0–3), varies within student.
  • cltype: class type (small / regular / regular with aide; reference regular), assigned by the experiment and varying within student; a 2-df within-school term.
  • ses: free-lunch status (reference not free lunch), varies within student.
  • sx, black: student-level.
  • schtype3: school type (city = inner-city + urban, suburb, rural); a 2-df between-school factor, which egsingle does not have.
  • fl_10: school percentage of free-lunch measurements in units of 10 points; a continuous between-school term.

Rare categories were merged so that resampled designs rarely lose a factor level (only 7 of 80 schools are urban; about 65 students are neither white nor black). Replicates that still lose a level are counted as failed fits; the student id is made unique within school because 446 students appear in more than one school.

Apart from yrs, every effect is small, and the between-school effects (schtype3, fl_10) are near zero. This tests the intervals in the near-null regime, which is rarer in egsingle.

4 Confidence interval coverage

As for egsingle: n_schools \(\in \{15, 100\}\) × n_per_site \(\in \{25, 200\}\), 1000 replicates per cell (seed 2027), intervals from resi()’s internal .resi_ci_mixed() with the model-based and CR2 (school-clustered) covariances and the normal, QF and CF methods, scored against \(S_m\) and \(S_{\text{Lyu}}\). Grey band: \(0.95 \pm 1.96\) Monte Carlo SE. Solid lines are between-school terms.

Coverage of S_m and S_Lyu by method (nominal 0.95; Monte Carlo SE 0.007)

5 Interpretation

The methods behave on STAR as they did on egsingle. One regime that egsingle did not test (a very large between-school RESI with few schools) exposes a small-n_schools limitation of the normal interval.

  • Point-estimate calibration.
    • Fixed effects: model SE / MC SD is 0.86–1.05. Values below 0.95 occur only for between-school terms at n_schools = 15.
    • Variance components: relative bias within ±3%.
    • Within-school RESI: on the Lyu limit at every n_per_site.
    • Between-school terms: the scaled MC SD exceeds the Lyu limiting SE (1.6–1.7 at n_per_site = 25, about 1.07 at 200), and the excess follows the design-averaged ticks. The RESI means follow the fixed-m bands \(S_m\).
    • This is the same finite-m estimand gap as for size_100/lowinc_10 in egsingle (school-level precision \(g/(\tau^2 + \sigma^2_w/m)\)).
  • Failed fits. 2–3% of replicates at n_schools = 15 lose a school-type level and are dropped (n_success). None are lost at n_schools >= 60.
  • CI coverage of \(S_m\), model-based covariance.
    • Coefficients (normal): 0.92–0.97 at n_schools = 15 and 0.94–0.97 at 100, except the intercept.
    • ANOVA terms with QF: 0.92–0.99. The normal ANOVA interval undercovers the small within-school terms at n_schools = 15 (sx 0.84, black 0.82, ses 0.88) and sx at n_schools = 100, n_per_site = 25 (0.81). QF and CF fix this, as in egsingle.
    • The near-null between-school terms (schtype3, fl_10, \(|S| < 0.07\)) are conservative (0.95–0.99), as expected for intervals near the boundary.
  • The intercept at n_schools = 15 covers at only about 0.77–0.79.
    • The STAR intercept RESI is very large (\(S_m \approx 8\)–10, against about 0.2 in egsingle). Its estimator scales like \(1/\hat\tau_{\text{school}}\), and with 15 schools \(\hat\tau\) is very uncertain. The sampling distribution is therefore right-skewed, and the delta-method SD underestimates the MC SD by about 20%.
    • At n_schools = 100 the intercept covers \(S_m\) at 0.94–0.95. Its \(S_{\text{Lyu}}\) coverage is low (0.36 at n_per_site = 25, 0.90 at 200), because the fixed-m gap (8.4 vs 10.6) is large relative to the interval width.
    • A skewness-aware or \(t_{g-1}\)-based interval (review question 4 of notes/resi_mixed_ci.qmd) would be the natural remedy. The current defaults were not changed.
  • CI coverage, CR2 covariance. As in egsingle: 0.86–0.94 for coefficients at n_schools = 15, where the estimated SD is up to 38% too small (few clusters), and 0.92–0.96 at n_schools = 100. The intercept is about 0.78 and 0.90.
  • \(S_{\text{Lyu}}\) coverage equals the \(S_m\) coverage for within-school terms and for the near-null between-school terms (whose fixed-m gap is tiny relative to the interval width). It drops for the intercept, as above.

Nothing in the methods needed to change for this dataset. The only dataset-specific code is the data preparation in tests/star_data.R. The terms, their levels (between/within) and all targets are derived from the fitted model by the shared package and library code.
